question: Henry Vivian Derozio is related to which of the following movement?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Young Bengal Movement**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Henry Vivian Derozio was a prominent social reformer and teacher in early 19th century Bengal, associated with the **Young Bengal Movement**.
 
• The Young Bengal Movement was characterized by its advocacy for **rationalism, liberty, equality, and freedom of thought**.
 
• Derozio instilled progressive ideas among his students at Hindu College, Calcutta, encouraging them to question societal norms and practices.
 
• He and his followers were influenced by the ideals of the **French Revolution** and sought to promote scientific thinking and secularism.
 
• The movement played a significant role in the **Bengal Renaissance**, laying the groundwork for future social reform initiatives in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Young Bengal Movement:**

 
 
• It emerged in Bengal during the 1820s and 1830s under the leadership of Henry Vivian Derozio.
 
• The followers of Derozio were called "Derozians," and they aimed to reform Indian society by promoting **modern education and critical thinking**.
 
• The movement emphasized the importance of **abolishing superstitions and social evils**, such as caste discrimination and sati.
 
 
 
• **Bengal Renaissance:**
 
 
• The Bengal Renaissance was a period of **cultural, social, and intellectual awakening** in Bengal during the 19th and early 20th centuries.
 
• It included contributions from reformers like Raja Ram Mohan Roy, Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, and Derozio.
 
• The Renaissance fostered a shift from traditional practices to modern ideas of equality, education, and rationalism.
 
 
 
• **Henry Vivian Derozio:**
 
 
• Derozio was born in 1809 and was of Portuguese descent; he is considered one of the earliest **Indian advocates of liberalism**.
 
• He taught at Hindu College, where he inspired students to challenge orthodox views and embrace progressive ideals.
 
• Despite his early death at the age of 22 in 1831, his ideas had a lasting impact on Indian society.
 
 
 
• **French Revolution Influence:**
 
 
• The Young Bengal Movement drew inspiration from the **ideals of the French Revolution**, including liberty, equality, and fraternity.
 
• These principles were applied to challenge traditional social hierarchies and foster intellectual freedom.
